name: Aerobloc Candelaria
description: A sixty-year-old residential aerobloc, forty-one households, hanging over the Austin/Garfield seam. Launched 2166 on a first-generation eigenlift frame; the frame is aging out of coherence faster than the housing co-op can fund recalibration, and the bloc is on a public descent schedule toward the 320-meter ceiling of The Low — where governance ends, insurance voids, and salvage law applies. Its altitude is painted on the commons wall and repainted lower most Mondays. Keel corridor runs bow to stern with forty years of handhold wear; the commons is the old launch bay. Water tanks migrate quadrant to quadrant on the ballast engineer's schedule. The bloc lists faintly to port after any jettison until trim catches up — residents feel the floor change underfoot and know what it means.
demographics: Forty-one households, ~130 residents, Ubiquitous Diaspora mix; three generations aboard in some lines. Working bracket: textile repair, machining, tether maintenance, transit work.
economy: Housing cooperative; shares by household. Air Tax bracket drops with altitude — every bracket line crossed cuts services and raises insurance until, at 320m, both stop.
power_structure: Co-op chair and standing rules; ballast engineer holds trim authority (schedule and jettison ledger); governor automaton Almagre enforces trim limits. AshgraveMaterials holds a standing structured-salvage offer, whole-bloc only.

atmosphere.sensory: Frame hum through the deck plates, lower after each jettison. Chalk marks on load points. The faint permanent list. Wind harmonics in the tether stays. The smell of the commons: machine oil, textile sizing, four decades of cooking in one ventilation loop.
atmosphere.mood: A house deciding how to land.
